title: RFID Hang Tag — Item-Level UHF Hang-Swing Tag for Apparel, Footwear and Retail
summary: RFID hang tags laminate a GS1 EPC Gen2v2 UHF inlay (Impinj M730 / M750 / M800, NXP UCODE 9) into a coated-paper, polyester or PVC hang-swing card with a string or plastic loop, pre-printed with brand / size / price artwork. They replace barcode-only hang-swings across apparel, footwear, accessories and general merchandise, delivering item-level inventory accuracy, source-tagging-aligned loss prevention, and BOPIS / ship-from-store fulfilment — without changing the existing hang-swing process on the supplier sewing floor.

brief.label: Form factor
items: Coated-paper / polyester / PVC card 40-80 mm × 20-40 mm, 0.3-0.8 mm thick, 1.5-3.5 g mass including string loop.
Hole punch Ø 4-6 mm for cotton string / plastic loop / swiftach attachment; standard retail pre-print zone 30 × 40 mm.

brief.label: Air-interface envelope
items: UHF 860-960 MHz — ISO 18000-63 / GS1 EPC Gen2v2 (Impinj M730 / M750 / M800, NXP UCODE 9, Alien Higgs-9).
Optional EAS AM 58 kHz or RF 8.2 MHz integration for dual-tech source-tagging; UHF + EAS sit on the same card without interference.

brief.label: Inlay chemistry
items: Aluminium or copper etched antenna on PET carrier; wet inlay adhesive for hang-card lamination.
Impinj M750 + NXP UCODE 9 small-footprint inlays (Mini / Short-dipole) for jewellery, footwear and small-accessory hang-swings where card area is ≤ 30 × 15 mm.

brief.label: Read-range envelope
items: 3-6 m on garment / textile / shoe packaging at +30 dBm handheld and +33 dBm portal reader with 6 dBic antenna.
Dense-population 200-500 items / rail at ≥ 99 % first-pass read in cycle-count sweep per RAIN RFID Alliance retail pilot benchmarks.

brief.label: Print + encode workflow
items: In-line printer / encoder (Zebra ZT411R, SATO CL4NX Plus, Avery 64-06 RFID) writes EPC (SGTIN-96) and prints brand / size / price / barcode on the card in a single pass at 100-150 mm/s.
EPC encoded per GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0 with the brand's GS1 Company Prefix; item GTIN + serial builds the SGTIN.

brief.label: Retail ecosystem integration
items: ARTS (Association for Retail Technology Standards) data model for POS / merchandising / replenishment events.
EPCIS 2.0 event stream into merchandising ERP, omnichannel OMS and RAIN RFID Alliance Retail Code of Conduct analytics.

brief.label: Store-floor process
items: Handheld cycle-count sweep by store associate 5,000-15,000 items in 45-60 minutes; replaces 4-8 hours of barcode scanning.
Smart fitting-room reader reads the hang-tag as the garment crosses the door, triggering style-card suggestions and stock check.

brief.label: Exit and loss-prevention
items: UHF overhead exit reader at 3-4 m mounting height generates shrink alert for unpaid SGTIN leaving the floor.
Dual-tech card carries source-tagged EAS for legacy pedestal integration during the transition to pure-UHF exit.

brief.label: Regulatory / transparency envelope
items: FCC Part 15.247 / §15.249 and RED 2014/53/EU governing the UHF handheld / portal reader paired with the hang-tag.
EU 2023/988 General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) digital product information hooks; FTC 16 CFR Part 303 care-label + country-of-origin on the hang-card print zone.

brief.label: Sustainability and disposal
items: Coated-paper card is FSC / PEFC chain-of-custody; PET inlay carrier and aluminium antenna recyclable along the paper fibre stream in separation-optimised MRFs.
PVC-free variant available for brands aligned with Higg Index / ZDHC programmes; REACH + RoHS 3 cleared across the SKU family.

brief.label: Integration and lock
items: Factory TID per ISO 18000-63 read-only; EPC locked with lock / permalock at source print / encode to prevent post-encode tamper.
NDEF / user-memory payload (NTAG 424 DNA SUN in dual-frequency variants) for consumer tap-authenticate / loyalty at POS.

heroPoints: GS1 SGTIN-96 encoded at source — item-level inventory accuracy measured at 98 %+ on the store floor versus 65-75 % under barcode-only cycle counting.
Source-tagging at the supplier sewing floor — brand / size / price / EPC printed + encoded in one pass on Zebra / SATO / Avery RFID printers at 100-150 mm/s.
Dual-tech UHF + EAS card option bridges legacy pedestal to pure-UHF exit — zero-disruption loss-prevention transition across a retail estate.

sections.title: Why the hang-tag is still the point where retail RFID enters the supply chain
bullets: Apparel, footwear and general-merchandise items already carry a hang-swing card at the supplier sewing floor; adding an RFID inlay to the same card turns source-tagging into a zero-marginal process change.

Item-level inventory accuracy under barcode-only cycle counting plateaus at 65-75 % because each read is a manual line-of-sight scan; RFID hang-tag sweeps reach 98 %+ first-pass accuracy, unlocking BOPIS / ship-from-store fulfilment promises that the stock data actually can support.

Retail shrinkage across North America and Europe sits at 1.5-2.0 % of sales; dual-tech UHF + EAS hang-tags at source give store-exit alerts tied to the SGTIN rather than a generic EAS pip, lifting recovery and audit quality.
RAIN RFID Alliance retail pilots report 30-60 % out-of-stock reductions once the store is dense-tagged at item level and the cycle-count cadence drops from weekly-hours to daily-minutes.

FTC 16 CFR Part 303 care-label / country-of-origin information and EU 2023/988 GPSR digital-information hooks live on the same hang-card, aligning compliance print and RFID source-tag in one artefact.

sections.title: Barcode-only, dual-tech hang-tag or pure-UHF hang-tag — what actually changes
bullets: Barcode-only hang-tag — line-of-sight scan, 1-3 s per item, cycle count at 3-8 hours per 1,000 SKUs; no real-time store inventory signal; loss prevention is a generic pedestal alarm.

Dual-tech UHF + EAS hang-tag — same 1-pass source-print, adds SGTIN-encoded cycle count at 3-5 seconds per rail of 100 items and exit-SGTIN-alert for shrinkage investigation, while still driving existing AM 58 kHz / RF 8.2 MHz pedestals.

Pure-UHF hang-tag — exit pedestal is replaced by an overhead UHF reader; EPCIS event stream becomes the sole audit trail for the item on the store floor; highest analytical value, lowest legacy-hardware drag.
Brands typically move barcode → dual-tech → pure-UHF over 18-30 months, keeping the existing supplier printing process constant and replacing the store exit hardware on a rolling basis.
Retail pilots consistently find the biggest single lift from the SGTIN encode itself rather than the exit hardware — merchandise visibility on the floor drives the sales and margin lift.

before: 65-75 % item-level inventory accuracy; weekly multi-hour cycle counts required to recover.
Line-of-sight scan, 1-3 s per item; manual handheld sweep of a 5,000-SKU store takes 4-8 hours.
Generic EAS pedestal alarm with no tie to SGTIN; recovery investigation depends on CCTV review.
Omnichannel fulfilment promises (BOPIS, ship-from-store) unreliable because stock data is stale and inaccurate.
after: 98 %+ first-pass item-level inventory accuracy; daily 45-60 minute sweep sufficient to keep it there.
Handheld UHF sweep 100+ items / second; dense-pop 200-500 items / rail at ≥ 99 % first pass.
Overhead UHF exit alerts with the SGTIN leaving the floor; structured shrink investigation tied to the item.
Real-time store inventory signal feeds OMS with accurate promise-of-delivery for BOPIS and ship-from-store.

sections.title: Where RFID hang-tags earn their place in the catalogue
bullets: Apparel — branded garments sewn at Tier-2 suppliers; hang-tag is applied at the supplier sewing floor with an in-line Zebra / SATO / Avery RFID printer / encoder, SGTIN encoded per GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0 with the brand's Company Prefix.

Footwear — hang-tag attached to the lace / tongue / box, or packed inside the box with a windowed sleeve; small-footprint inlay (Impinj M750 Mini / NXP UCODE 9 Short-dipole) keeps the card under 30 × 15 mm.
Accessories, jewellery, eyewear — small hang-card with a short-dipole inlay; read range 1-2 m sufficient for a jewellery-counter tray scan and an exit UHF read.
General merchandise — toys, home-goods, sporting goods; hang-card is often already on the item for brand / size / price print, and the RFID inlay drops into the card stack with no new process step.

Multi-brand department store — source-tagging programme where each brand encodes its own SGTIN with its own Company Prefix; the retailer reads all brands on one store UHF estate with a single ARTS-aligned data model.
BOPIS / ship-from-store / buy-online-return-in-store — accurate store stock signal feeds OMS, so promise-of-delivery and cross-store rebalancing reflect reality rather than stale weekly cycle counts.

dataHighlight.heading: Out-of-stock reduction in RAIN RFID Alliance retail pilots
dataHighlight.text: RAIN RFID Alliance retail pilot case studies across 2018-2024 consistently report 30-60 % out-of-stock reduction and 2-10 % sales lift after item-level UHF source-tagging through the hang-tag, driven mainly by the step-change from 65-75 % to 98 %+ floor-level inventory accuracy and the resulting accuracy of BOPIS / ship-from-store promises.
dataHighlight.source: RAIN RFID Alliance Retail Vertical Working Group case studies 2018-2024 and the Auburn University RFID Lab 'Project Zipper' multi-year retail benchmark (2019-2023).

sections.title: How to roll out an RFID hang-tag programme without tearing up the supplier process
bullets: Keep the hang-card artwork and process at the supplier sewing floor constant; swap the paper stack for an inlay-laminated stack from the RFID tag supplier and specify the Zebra / SATO / Avery in-line RFID printer / encoder model.
Lock EPC encoding to GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0 with the brand's Company Prefix; every hang-tag carries an SGTIN-96, encoded and permalocked in-line at 100-150 mm/s.
Tie the EPCIS 2.0 event stream into OMS, merchandising ERP and loss-prevention analytics through an ARTS-aligned data model.
Transition loss-prevention in two steps: first, dual-tech UHF + EAS hang-tag with existing pedestals for SGTIN-aware alerts; second, overhead UHF exit reader as pedestals hit end-of-life.

Respect the RAIN RFID Alliance Retail Code of Conduct — the SGTIN does not carry PII, the store does not link the tag to a loyalty customer without opt-in, and the retailer publishes a privacy notice covering any tag-to-customer linkage.

Bring FSC / PEFC chain-of-custody certificates for the paper card, ZDHC / Higg artefacts for the laminate and a REACH / RoHS 3 DoC for the inlay into the supplier pack so sustainability audits pass alongside the technical audit.

items.label: Weeks 1-3 — tag + encode bench
items.text: Select inlay (Impinj M730 / M750 / M800, NXP UCODE 9, Alien Higgs-9) per category footprint; set up an RFID printer / encoder bench (Zebra ZT411R, SATO CL4NX Plus, Avery 64-06) and validate SGTIN encode + print at 100-150 mm/s with 100 % encode rate on 10,000 hang-tags.

items.label: Weeks 4-6 — supplier onboarding
items.text: Move printer / encoder into the Tier-2 supplier sewing floor; train operators; validate brand artwork + SGTIN encode pipeline end-to-end against the retailer OMS; dry-run 3-5 brand PO cycles.

items.label: Weeks 7-10 — store pilot
items.text: Roll 5-20 pilot stores with handheld UHF sweep, smart fitting-room reader and dual-tech exit pedestal; measure cycle-count time, accuracy uplift, out-of-stock reduction and shrink recovery against baseline.

items.label: Weeks 11-16 — OMS + loss-prevention cutover
items.text: Turn the EPCIS 2.0 event stream on as the source of truth for store-level inventory; OMS promise-of-delivery, BOPIS and ship-from-store now run against RFID-sourced stock; loss-prevention investigations attach the SGTIN to each incident.

items.label: Month 5+ — estate rollout
items.text: Programme experience across apparel + footwear + accessories hang-tag contributes the audit, refresh and onboarding patterns that inform this solution's operating playbook. scale from pilot stores to 500+ stores and 50-500 M hang-tags / year, migrate pedestals to pure-UHF exit on a rolling basis, and tie every SGTIN to RAIN RFID Alliance retail analytics, RoHS / REACH / ZDHC compliance evidence and an OMS omnichannel fulfilment SLA.

faq.question: Does the RFID hang-tag change the sewing-floor process for our Tier-2 suppliers?
faq.answer: No — the hang-swing artwork, card stock and string-loop attachment stay identical. The only change is that the paper stack loaded into the existing Zebra / SATO / Avery printer is an inlay-laminated stack; the printer model moves to the RFID-capable SKU (ZT411R, CL4NX Plus, 64-06), and the encode step adds the SGTIN alongside the existing barcode print at 100-150 mm/s, inside the same production-cycle budget.

faq.question: Can a single hang-tag drive both the existing EAS pedestals and a new UHF exit?
faq.answer: Yes — the dual-tech card carries both an AM 58 kHz or RF 8.2 MHz EAS element and an ISO 18000-63 UHF inlay; both technologies co-exist on the same card without interference. This lets the retailer keep existing pedestals live during an 18-30 month transition and swap them to overhead UHF readers on a rolling basis without re-tagging merchandise.

faq.question: How does the tag respect retail-customer privacy?
faq.answer: The SGTIN encoded on the hang-tag identifies the item, not the customer. The RAIN RFID Alliance Retail Code of Conduct is the reference framework: retailers do not link tag reads to a loyalty ID without explicit opt-in, publish a privacy notice at point of sale, and kill / deactivate or offer to remove the tag at checkout where local law requires it. Dual-frequency variants with NTAG 424 DNA SUN payloads follow the same consent-based model for consumer tap-authenticate experiences.

sources.label: GS1 EPC Radio-Frequency Identity Protocols — Generation-2 UHF RFID (EPC Gen2v2)
sources.note: Governs the UHF air interface and lock / permalock semantics used by the retail hang-tag inlay.

sources.label: GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0
sources.note: Spec for SGTIN-96 encoding used across apparel, footwear, accessories and general merchandise hang-tags.

sources.label: GS1 EPCIS 2.0 — Electronic Product Code Information Services
sources.note: Event-stream spec that the retail OMS / merchandising ERP subscribes to for item-level inventory events.

sources.label: RAIN RFID Alliance — Retail Code of Conduct
sources.note: Industry self-regulation covering data minimisation, notice, consent and disablement for consumer-facing UHF retail tags.

sources.label: ARTS — Association for Retail Technology Standards, Unified Point-of-Sale Data Model
sources.note: Retail data model that retailers map EPCIS item-level events into for merchandising and loss-prevention analytics.

sources.label: 47 CFR Part 15 — Radio Frequency Devices
sources.note: Subpart C §15.247 / §15.249 govern UHF handheld / portal readers paired with the hang-tag in the US.
